questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

He was so__** enraged**__** **at the article about him that he sued the newspaper.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Angered**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"enraged"** means to be extremely angry or furious. (क्रोधित)

 
 
• **Example: **His enraged response made it clear that he was deeply offended by the accusation.
 
 
 
• **"Angered" **refers to the state of being angry or showing strong displeasure. (गुस्से में)
 
 
• **Example: **She was angered by his rude comments during the meeting.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that a synonym for **'enraged' **is **'angered'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Angered**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• **Example:** The new policy generated a lot of discussion among the employees.
 
 
 
• **Determined **(दृढ़ निश्चयी): Having made a firm decision and being resolved not to change it.
 
 
• **Example: **She was determined to win the competition despite all odds.
 
 
 
• **Enhanced** (बढ़ाया हुआ): To intensify, increase, or further improve the quality, value, or extent of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The new software enhanced the performance of the computer system.

questions.question:
Recognise the sentence with the correct transitive verb form of break.

A. The cyclone broke the window. 

B. The window broke.

C. The cyclone caused the braking of window.

D. The cyclone caused the broken window.
questions.solution:
The correct option is: **2) A**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Option A: "The cyclone broke the window."** This sentence correctly uses the **transitive verb** **"broke,"** where **"the cyclone"** is the **subject**, **"broke"** is the **transitive verb**, and **"the window"** is the **object **of the **verb**. A **transitive verb **requires an **object **to complete its meaning, and here the window is the object that is being affected by the action of the verb "broke."
 
• **Option B:** **"The window broke." **This sentence uses the **intransitive form** of **"break"** because it does not have an object. The verb **"broke"** in this sentence is used **intransitively** to describe the window itself breaking, without any external agent causing the action. Therefore, this is not the correct choice when looking for a transitive verb form.
 
• **Option C:** **"The cyclone caused the braking of window." **This sentence attempts to use **"braking"** in a way that isn't grammatically correct in the context of the verb "break." The phrase "caused the braking" is awkward and unnatural, making this option incorrect.
 
• **Option D: "The cyclone caused the broken window."** This sentence uses a **passive structure** ("broken window"), which is not an example of a transitive verb. The phrase "caused the broken window" incorrectly uses the past participle form "broken" as an adjective, but it doesn't reflect the transitive verb "break."

Thus, **Option A** is the correct answer because it uses "broke" as a transitive verb with an object, which is the requirement in this case.

questions.question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.

options.text: By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **2) By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2** is grammatically correct because it uses the correct tense sequence.
 
• The phrase **"By the time we arrived"** uses the **past simple tense**, which is appropriate for an action that is completed before another action in the past.
 
• The phrase **"they had been waiting"** uses the **past perfect continuous tense**, indicating that their waiting started earlier and continued until the time we arrived.
 
• This combination of past simple and past perfect continuous is the correct way to show the sequence of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1: **"By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."

 
 
• This option incorrectly uses the present tense "arrive" instead of the past tense "arrived." Since the sentence talks about an event that happens before another event in the past, the past tense "arrived" is required.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."
 
 
• This option incorrectly uses "arrives", which is the present tense form for a singular subject (e.g., "he/she arrives"). Since the subject "we" is plural, the correct form should be "arrived" (past tense).
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."
 
 
• This option incorrectly uses "arriving", which is the present participle form. To show a completed action in the past, the correct form is "arrived" (past simple).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the ______ student of the class too.
questions.solution:
The correct option is: **1) most intelligent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is structured to convey that Prem is not just intelligent but the most intelligent in the entire class.
 
• This means that out of all the students, Prem stands out as the one with the highest degree of intelligence.
 
• When we are comparing more than two things or expressing the extreme degree of a particular quality, we use the **superlative form of the adjective**.
 
 
• **Example: **Among all the athletes, John is the most skilled.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, **"Most intelligent"** indicates that Prem is at the highest level of intelligence compared to all other students in the class.

Hence, the correct answer is: *Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the **most intelligent**__ student of the class too.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Why Other Options Are Incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 2:** **intelligently **– This is an adverb, and it modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. The sentence needs an adjective to describe Prem, not an adverb. So "intelligently" would not be grammatically appropriate.
 
• **Option 3: intelligent **– This is the positive form of the adjective. It only describes Prem as being intelligent but doesn't convey the idea that he is the best or most intelligent in comparison to others. It lacks the superlative quality that is essential for the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** **more intelligent** – This is the comparative form, used to compare two things or people. The sentence, however, is not comparing Prem to one other person but rather stating that Prem is the top student among all others. So, the comparative form is inappropriate here.
